content.page_summary: Discussion of echocardiographic parameters for assessment of right ventricular (RV) pressure overload in suspected pulmonary embolism (PE). Describes reduced TAPSE, Doppler tissue imaging, wall strain assessment, and limitations of echocardiography in haemodynamically stable patients. Figure 3 provides a graphic representation of transthoracic echocardiographic signs of RV overload with a list of abbreviations.
key_points: Decreased tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) may be present in PE patients.
Echocardiographic parameters of RV function derived from Doppler tissue imaging and wall strain assessment can be affected by acute PE but have low sensitivity as standalone findings.
Echocardiography is not mandatory for routine diagnostic workup in haemodynamically stable patients with suspected PE, although it may help in differential diagnosis of acute dyspnoea.
In suspected high-risk PE, absence of echocardiographic signs of RV overload or dysfunction makes PE as the cause of haemodynamic instability unlikely.
Echocardiography can aid differential diagnosis in shock by detecting pericardial tamponade, acute valvular dysfunction, severe LV dysfunction, aortic dissection, or hypovolaemia.
In haemodynamically compromised patients with suspected PE, unequivocal signs of RV pressure overload (e.g., 60/60 sign, McConnell sign, right-heart thrombus) are especially relevant.

abbreviations.AcT: Right ventricular outflow Doppler acceleration time

clinical_recommendations.stable_patients: Echocardiography not mandatory in routine workup for haemodynamically stable suspected PE, may be useful for differential diagnosis.
clinical_recommendations.high_risk_PE: In suspected high-risk PE, absence of RV overload/dysfunction on echocardiography practically excludes PE as cause of haemodynamic instability; echocardiography helpful to detect alternative causes of shock.
clinical_recommendations.haemodynamically_compromised: In compromised patients with suspected PE, unequivocal echocardiographic signs of RV pressure overload (60/60 sign, McConnell sign, right-heart thrombus) are especially important.
